methodology: Codex independently reopened the direct company, manager, counterparty and regulatory sources used in the list decision; verified the cited claims against retrieved content; recorded final URL, status, media type, byte length and SHA-256 where retrieval succeeded; and separately extracted the relevant ArcLight and regulatory PDF text. Search-result snippets were not treated as proposal evidence.

verifiedClaims: REC Solar rebranded as REC Power on June 30, 2026.
The announcement describes a continuing operating company rather than a new acquisition or separate platform.
REC Power remained an ArcLight Capital Partners portfolio company and operated a nationwide multi-technology distributed-power platform.
REC Power stated on July 28, 2026 that it is owned by ArcLight Capital Partners.
REC Power described itself as a nationwide independent power producer that finances, owns and operates distributed power assets.
The completed 68 MW acquisition took the operating portfolio above 410 MW across 25 states.
The business traces its founding to REC Solar in 1997.
REC Power is the current public identity of the continuing commercial distributed-power platform.
The page supports the platform's nationwide distributed-power operating model.
Duke announced the definitive ArcLight agreement on July 5, 2023.
The $364 million enterprise-value transaction included REC Solar operating assets, development pipeline and O&M portfolio.
Duke described ArcLight as an infrastructure investor and the transaction as creation of a standalone renewable platform.
Duke completed the sale on October 4, 2023.
The buyer was an investment fund managed by ArcLight Capital Partners.
The closing included REC Solar's operating assets, development pipeline and O&M portfolio.
ArcLight calls the Duke portfolio acquisition part of Fund VII's REC Solar investment.
The page distinguishes the manager-level REC Solar investment from more than 160 individual underlying projects.
The report defines Fund VII as ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII, L.P.
The portfolio appendix lists REC Solar as a Renewable investment of Fund VII.
A downstream REC project ownership chain terminates at ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII, L.P.
The filing expressly defines ArcLight Capital as ArcLight Capital Partners, LLC and identifies it as Fund VII's investment adviser.
The filing does not prove a 100% platform stake or identify the contractual platform acquisition vehicle.
ArcLight's live investment table still lists REC Solar as Current in Renewables.
The modal's placeholder copy and inconsistent 2021 date were rejected and are not used.

sources.notes: The model found a cached/indexed copy, but the direct ArcLight URL returned 404 during Codex verification. The final proposal therefore relies on the working 2025 ArcLight ESG report, portfolio-services page and regulatory filing instead.

modelEvidenceCorrections.claim: A project-chain 100% ownership disclosure establishes ArcLight's platform-level stake.
modelEvidenceCorrections.reason: The regulatory percentages apply to downstream project entities, not necessarily REC Power's platform capitalization. The structured stake remains null.

modelEvidenceCorrections.claim: AL REC Holdings, AL Solar Acquirer or a Fund VII AIV should be recorded as the platform acquisition vehicle.
modelEvidenceCorrections.reason: Reviewed sources do not identify any one downstream entity as the contractual buyer of the REC Solar operating company. The vehicle remains null.

modelEvidenceCorrections.claim: ArcLight's investment-table modal proves a 2021 REC Solar investment date.
modelEvidenceCorrections.reason: The modal also contains placeholder content and conflicts with direct 2023 announcement and closing evidence.

modelEvidenceCorrections.claim: DigitalBridge's signed acquisition of ArcLight creates a pending REC Power owner.
modelEvidenceCorrections.reason: That transaction concerns the investment manager and does not disclose a transfer of Fund VII's REC Power interest.

modelEvidenceCorrections.claim: The legacy 2025 scale milestone has a supported 2025 date.
modelEvidenceCorrections.reason: The legacy page redirects. The proposal moves scale into sourced current description language and uses dated June and July 2026 milestones.

exitSearchConclusion: No REC Power-level completed sale, signed pending exit, dissolution or successor platform was identified through 2026-08-15. Current company and manager sources support continuing ArcLight ownership. The manager-level DigitalBridge transaction does not create a PortCo ownership change.
